patch_description:
Crossover of the two strongest prior seeds. Both top performers converged on
a design with very few distinct circuit parameters and a shared-generator
multi-shell entangler: the 2-parameter "theta_ry / theta_z" seed (score
0.61, sharing theta_z between the RZ layer and a 3-shell CRZ entangler) beat
both the 3-parameter shell design (score 0.59) and the current 5-parameter
alternating-rotation design (score 0.52). This confirms the stated scoring
rule that fewer distinct trainable parameters always scores higher, and that
generator sharing between local rotations and entanglers is a particularly
effective way to get "free" expressivity without new parameters.

This candidate keeps the winning 2-parameter skeleton (global RY = theta_ry,
global RZ = theta_z, entangling shells reusing theta_z) and reinforces it
with two zero-cost additions, both achieved purely through parameter reuse
so N_PARAMS stays at 2 distinct circuit angles (4 total with gain/bias):

1. A long-range antipodal CRY shell that reuses theta_ry (rather than adding
   a third parameter), giving the entangling graph a second independent
   generator type (Y-controlled as well as Z-controlled rotations) which
   should let the circuit express correlations that a single CRZ-only
   entangler cannot reach, directly targeting the two-qubit readout
   observable and the worst-group margin.
2. A final global RY "mixer" layer, again reusing theta_ry, giving the
   circuit one extra degree of freedom to rotate the resulting Bloch vectors
   into alignment with the fixed readout observable right before
   measurement — the same trick that helped the highest-margin seed, but
   without spending a new parameter name since it's tied to theta_ry.

Net effect: still exactly 2 distinct circuit parameters (the maximum
parameter economy demonstrated to work well), but a richer, two-generator
entangling structure plus an output-aligning mixer, aimed at raising the
worst-group margin and reducing the train/validation gap relative to both
prior seeds, while keeping convergence fast since the parameter count is
minimal.
